detail: a faced copper printing plate resting on green baize, its surface cut with a single surveyed territory in clean reversed lines, the burin marks confident and evenly spaced, the plate kept under a weighted cloth because every copy in the world is struck from it

evidence.quote: The model governs and the scaffolding becomes a sketch of what to implement.

facts.extent: a thick copper plate the size of an open folio, bevelled at the edges
facts.scale_ref: stored flat in a shallow oak drawer, one plate per charted territory
facts.material: faced rolled copper, burin-cut, inked in bistre and wiped clean between strikings
facts.state: authoritative and unamended; corrections are re-engraved into the plate, never pencilled onto a print

note: Code that declares a structure already observed, and from which all working copies derive. The plate is the single source of truth: a print carries authority only because of the plate beneath it. This is the difference between legislation and observation. You cannot engrave what has not been surveyed — a plate cut from a Field Sketch merely freezes the sketch's guesses at full authority. Corrections amend the plate and the next striking reflects them; no one edits a print and calls the map fixed. Flattening a scattered structure into one clean contract is what engraving produces, not what it sets out to do. Every plate carries the standing tier 'canon'.
